draft.title: Ways of organising ideas
card: Writers organise ideas so a reader can follow them. Three common ways are time order, cause and effect, and groups and types.
Ideas come in the order they happened or should be done. Words such as first, next, then and finally are common. Recounts and instructions often use it.
Ideas link what made something happen (the cause) to what happened as a result (the effect). Words such as because, so and as a result are common.
Ideas are sorted into groups, and each group is described in turn. Words such as one kind, another type and some are common. A text about pets might have one part on dogs and one on cats.
draft.remember: Ask how the ideas are linked: by when, by why, or by kind.

a.q: A text explains how to make a paper plane. It begins with folding the paper in half, then folding the corners, and ends with the wings. How is it organised?
opts: In time order, one step after another
By cause and effect, as each fold causes the next
By groups and types of paper plane
By sorting the folds into kinds of wing
a.why: The steps are given in the order they are done, so the text uses time order. Each fold does follow another, but the text does not explain why one thing makes another happen, so it is not cause and effect.
a.clue: Look at the order the steps are done in.

b.q: A paragraph says that heavy rain fell on Ballarat for three days. As a result, the creek overflowed, and so some roads were closed. How is it organised?
opts: By cause and effect, each event leading to the next
In time order, because it mentions three days
By groups and types of flood damage
By cause and effect, with the rain as the only link
b.why: Words such as as a result and so link the rain to the overflow and then to the closures, so each event is the effect of the one before. It mentions three days, but the main link between events is cause and effect, so time order is the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Look at the linking words as a result and so.

a.best: In time order, one step after another

b.best: By cause and effect, each event leading to the next
